name: @w6w-apps/streamtime
description: Read and write Streamtime jobs, job items, quotes, invoices, logged time and expenses, and run filtered searches and reports against the Public API.

w6w.longDescription:
Streamtime is job tracking and project management for creative agencies: the money side of a studio — jobs, phases, job items, the people and roles booked against them, quotes, invoices, and the time and expenses everybody logs — lives in one place.

The Public API is shaped unlike a typical REST surface, and this app is built around what it actually does. Only four of the resource collections answer a list request at all (branches, rate cards, roles, users); companies, jobs, logged time and logged expenses are create-only at the collection level and readable one id at a time. Getting a list of them means going through POST /search, a generic query endpoint with its own filter-expression language, which this app exposes verbatim — along with GET /search/setup and GET /report/setup, the two metadata endpoints Streamtime tells callers to fetch first. POST /report covers the aggregation questions the same way: totals, averages and grouped breakdowns without pulling every record back.

Beyond search, the app covers the full documented write surface — creating and updating companies, contacts, jobs, phases, job items, milestones, item roles, item users and sub-items, logging time in bulk, logging and updating expenses, creating invoice payments, and managing labels — plus the nesting underneath a job item, which is where agency scheduling actually lives. Quote and invoice documents come back as HTML or base64-encoded PDF.

Health checks track Streamtime's own status page (its API component), probe the credential with the organisation read, and record that Streamtime publishes no quota or rate-limit surface at all. The credential probe deliberately classifies from the response body rather than the status code, because Streamtime answers an identical 401 body for a missing token, an invalid token, and a path that does not exist.
